sec1.titulo: The three seconds after you stop
abertura: You gave your three minutes. You stop. Somebody raises a hand.
Mark the three statements that are true of a good answer under those conditions.

itens.t: It starts before you have decided the whole answer.
It checks what was asked when the question is not clear.
It never says "I do not have that number".
It can disagree, as long as it says why.
It is longer than the part of the talk it refers to.
It answers whatever the person seemed to mean.

sec1.rationale: Two of the wrong ones are the same mistake in different clothes: answering the question you imagined instead of the one that was asked. Checking costs eight seconds and saves the whole answer.

nota.titulo: Why this comes right after lesson 3
nota.texto: In lesson 3 you closed by saying what neither version answered — which regulator. This is that meeting, three seconds later, and Diane, who chairs the board, asks exactly that. Two more hands go up after hers: Ray, who runs the program office, and Nadia, who owns the engineering budget.

abertura: Choose the better reading for each expression. You will hear or need all six.

itens.t: That is a fair question
alts: I agree with the person
I am taking it seriously, and I am about to answer
itens.ok: I am taking it seriously, and I am about to answer

itens.t: Let me take that in two parts
alts: the question has two questions inside it
I will answer half of it
itens.ok: the question has two questions inside it

itens.t: If I understand you correctly
alts: I am checking before I answer
I did not listen
itens.ok: I am checking before I answer

itens.t: Short answer
alts: I am cutting the conversation
I am giving the direct answer first, and the detail after
itens.ok: I am giving the direct answer first, and the detail after

itens.t: I would push back on that
alts: I refuse to answer
I disagree, and I am about to say why
itens.ok: I disagree, and I am about to say why

itens.t: I do not have that with me
alts: I am not guessing; the number comes later, from me
I do not know and will not find out
itens.ok: I am not guessing; the number comes later, from me

nota.texto: That is a fair question and let me take that in two parts buy you four or five seconds while you decide the shape of the answer. That is not stalling — it is what everyone fluent does, and it is why they never seem to hesitate.

sec3.titulo: What the question is really after
abertura: Six questions from a real review meeting. What does each one actually want?

itens.t: "Which market asked first?"
"Is December a hard date?"
"How is that not gold-plating?"
"How many cases were declined last quarter?"
"Are you asking us to approve the delay today?"
"Would you bet the launch on that assumption?"

nota.titulo: Each kind wants a different first sentence
nota.texto: A fact wants the number, or an honest “I will send it”. A decision wants a yes or a no before the reasoning. A challenge wants you to name the assumption out loud — and then defend it.

sec4.titulo: The one that is not clear

doc.texto: “I want to come back to the December thing. I am not sure I follow. Is that a hard date, or is it more of a, you know, a direction? Because we have said December before.”

abertura: Mark the three statements that are true of this question.

itens.t: It contains a complaint that is not stated as one.
It asks for a fact.
It offers you two answers and expects one of them.
The last sentence is the real question.
It is hostile.
It can be answered without checking anything.

sec4.rationale: "We have said December before" is where the question actually lives. Answering only the hard-date/direction pair leaves the complaint on the table, and it will come back.

nota.titulo: Vague is not the same as hostile
nota.texto: Ray is not aggressive at all — and his is the most dangerous of the three, because you can answer it fully and still not have answered it. Nadia's, which comes last, is the hostile one, and it is easier.

abertura: Each opening starts a check. Complete it so that the check actually narrows the question.

itens.t: If I understand you correctly, you are asking
alts: whether we can commit to December, not whether December is possible
if I am sure
about the model
itens.ok: whether we can commit to December, not whether December is possible

itens.t: Let me take that in two parts:
alts: the past and the future
the date, and why the last one moved
the model and the market
itens.ok: the date, and why the last one moved

itens.t: Before I answer — do you mean
alts: anything in particular?
the requirement itself, or the fact that it is not published yet?
the launch?
itens.ok: the requirement itself, or the fact that it is not published yet?

itens.t: Short answer: yes, December is a commitment.
alts: The longer answer is why the last date moved.
I will send you the details.
That is all I can say.
itens.ok: The longer answer is why the last date moved.

itens.t: I would push back on the word gold-plating,
alts: because six weeks is short
because the requirement is drafted, not absent
because you are wrong
itens.ok: because the requirement is drafted, not absent

nota.titulo: The check has to cost the other person something
nota.texto: A check that can be answered with “yes, exactly” has done nothing. A good check makes the other person choose — and the choice is what tells you which answer to give.

abertura: Complete the answer. Every gap is one of the six expressions from activity 2.
This is Nadia's question, the hostile one. Write it once here and you will have it in the room.
itens: {That is a fair question|180px}, and I want to answer it properly.
{Let me take that in two parts|220px}: what the requirement is, and why six weeks.
{If I understand you correctly|210px}, the objection is that nothing has been published yet.
{I would push back on that|190px}, because a draft that three regulators are consulting on is not nothing.
{Short answer|140px}: I am not building for a rumor. And on the exact wording, {I do not have that with me|200px} — I will send it today.

I would push back on that

nota.titulo: This is the answer you will give in class
nota.texto: Five sentences, and the hardest question in the room is handled. In class you will say it without the text in front of you, and with twenty seconds less than you would like.

gs4.prompt: Listen to all three once. Mark the two that are true.

itens.t: One of the three is not really asking a question.
All three are about the December date.
One of them asks for something you did not say in your three minutes.
They all agree with your recommendation.
The last one is the friendliest.

gs4.rationale: The third is a challenge dressed as a question, and the first asks for the fact your talk left out. Hearing which is which, before answering, is the whole lesson.

itens.t: Gives you a number you did not have.
Asks you to confirm the recommendation.
Calls the six weeks unnecessary work.
Offers you two possible answers to choose from.
Says that this date has been promised before.
Asks which market moved first.

nota.texto: Not one of the three asks whether you stand by the recommendation — and that is normal. A room that is questioning the reasoning has already heard the ask. Restating it is the most common way to waste your first sentence.

itens.t: "That is a fair question."
"Do you mean the requirement, or the fact that it is not published?"
"I would push back on the word gold-plating."
"Let me take that in two parts."
"If I understand you correctly, you are asking about the commitment."
"A draft under consultation is not a rumor."

nota.texto: The two in the first column say nothing at all about the content — and that is their job. They give you four seconds to choose the shape of the answer, and they cost the room nothing. Fluent speakers use them constantly; it is part of why they never seem to search.

abertura: A quick reference to the situation and the language you used.

callout.titulo: Why write the check and not the answer
callout.texto: The answer changes with the day. The check is the same every time, and it is the part that does not come out under pressure unless you have said it before.
